feature1.prompt:
Optimize multiple AlterFooTogether operations into one

Hi,
In #31503 we split the AlterFooTogether (AlterUniqueTogether and AlterIndexTogether) operations into two types of operations. First, a migration will have operations to remove constraints, and then other operations add the new constraints. This allows field alterations to work as expected during in between operations. In some cases, this introduced two operations that can actually easily be reduced to one. See for instance the test case example:

 operations = [
   migrations.AlterUniqueTogether(
     name='mymodel',
     unique_together=set(),
   ),
   migrations.AlterIndexTogether(
     name='mymodel',
     index_together=set(),
   ),
   migrations.AlterUniqueTogether(
     name='mymodel',
     unique_together={("col",)},
   ),
   migrations.AlterIndexTogether(
     name='mymodel',
     index_together={("col",)},
   ),
 ]

should be optimized to

 operations = [
   migrations.AlterUniqueTogether(
     name='mymodel',
     unique_together={("col",)},
   ),
   migrations.AlterIndexTogether(
     name='mymodel',
     index_together={("col",)},
   ),
 ]

so that we don't do two operations on each constraint, but only one.
feature1.hint_texts: This feature focuses on refactoring the internal logic of how multiple AlterFooTogether operations are reduced. You should introduce or update the mechanism that determines if operations can be merged – for example, by introducing a helper method that checks if an operation can be reduced through. The reduce method in the operations should be modified to use this new check. Use the provided example to ensure that when operations are applied, duplicate constraint changes are merged into a single operation.
feature1.entrypoint: File: django/db/migrations/operations/models.py. Modify the 'reduce' method to invoke the new reduction check and implement the new 'can_reduce_through' method that determines if an operation references the model and can be merged.
